input.label: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
input.reasoning_summary:
After investigating potential challenges to the initial verdict, all three hypotheses were refuted:

H1 (Did Amazon report Q4 2026 results?): REFUTED. The retrieved evidence shows Amazon's most recent filings as of the evidence cutoff date (2026-11-01) were the Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-10-30, period ending 2026-09-30) and Q2 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-07-31, period ending 2026-06-30). No filing containing actual Q4 2026 results was found. The numeric check also returned UNVERIFIABLE with issue "PERIOD_NOT_AVAILABLE:2026-12-31".

H2 (Does Amazon use a non-calendar fiscal year?): REFUTED. E12 explicitly states "FORM 10-K For the Fiscal Year Ended December 31, 2025", confirming Amazon's fiscal year aligns with the calendar year. Therefore, Q4 2026 would end on December 31, 2026, which had not yet occurred as of the evidence cutoff date of 2026-11-01.

H3 (Were preliminary Q4 2026 results released early?): REFUTED. E13 and E14 show that on October 29, 2026, Amazon provided forward-looking guidance for Q4 2026, stating "Net sales are expected to be between $240.0 billion and $247.0 billion, or to grow between 12% and 16% compared with fourth quarter 2025." This is explicitly labeled as forward-looking guidance reflecting "expectations," not actual or preliminary results.

The evidence review confirms that E6 and E13 (the guidance statements) are FORWARD_LOOKING and marked as RELATED_NOT_DECIDING, not ENTAILS. They represent expectations issued before Q4 2026 ended, not actual reported results.

The claim requires actual reported net sales figures for Q4 2026 (quarter ended December 31, 2026) to verify year-over-year growth. Since the evidence cutoff date is 2026-11-01 and Q4 2026 ends on 2026-12-31, the quarter had not yet concluded and actual results would not be available in any filing. The verdict remains INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.
